## Claims
- [source-backed] Schur functions are homogeneous of partition weight, and the Grassmannian quotient inherits this grading. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 263-269]
- [source-backed] The involution \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) is a ring involution. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 481-485]
- [proved] The requested corollary
  \[
  J_v/A_+J_v\cong J_{v^\vee}/A_+J_{v^\vee}
  \]
  is an integral graded isomorphism; it preserves torsion subgroups and every degreewise rank.

## Strategy
Let \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), \(A^\vee=\Lambda/I_{q,r}\), and let
\[
\Omega:A\overset{\sim}{\longrightarrow}A^\vee,\qquad
\overline{s_\lambda}\longmapsto\overline{s_{\lambda'}}.
\]
Accepted quotient conjugation makes this well-defined, and accepted ideal correspondence gives
\(\Omega(J_v)=J_{v^\vee}\).

Since \(|\lambda'|=|\lambda|\), \(\Omega\) is graded. Therefore it maps the positive-degree ideal onto the positive-degree ideal:
\[
\Omega(A_+)=A^\vee_+.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\Omega(A_+J_v)=\Omega(A_+)\Omega(J_v)
=A^\vee_+J_{v^\vee}.
\]
Thus \(\Omega|_{J_v}\) descends to an integral graded isomorphism
\[
\bar\Omega:J_v/A_+J_v\overset{\sim}{\longrightarrow}
J_{v^\vee}/A^\vee_+J_{v^\vee}.
\]

For every degree \(d\), its restriction is an isomorphism of finitely generated abelian groups
\[
\bar\Omega_d:(J_v/A_+J_v)_d\overset{\sim}{\longrightarrow}
(J_{v^\vee}/A^\vee_+J_{v^\vee})_d.
\]
Hence it restricts to an isomorphism on integral torsion subgroups and induces equality of free ranks:
\[
\operatorname{Tor}(Q_d)\cong\operatorname{Tor}(Q^\vee_d),
\qquad
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Z}Q_d=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Z}Q^\vee_d.
\]
Therefore every certified degreewise indecomposables computation transfers unchanged, including torsion factors and ranks, to the conjugate case.

## Gaps
None, conditional on the accepted quotient-conjugation and ideal-correspondence results.
